# messq_auth_add

See `messq help exit-codes` for the exit-code contract.

## messq auth add

mint one token, print its credential once, store its hash

### Synopsis

Mint a fresh credential msq1_<id>_<secret>, append its SHA-256 line to the
--auth-file, and print the credential to stdout EXACTLY ONCE. Nobody can show
it again; if it is lost, remove the line by hand and add anew with the same
id — renaming ids invalidates credentials by design (the hash covers them).
The file keeps mode 0600 and single-line appends leave every prior token
intact. Duplicate ids and duplicate hashes are refused before anything is
written: two ids sharing one credential would make events.actor ambiguous.
Roles are publish, consume and admin — plain sets, no hierarchy — scoped to
comma-separated stream patterns ('orders' is exact, 'orders*' covers the
family including orders.dlq).

```
messq auth add [flags]
```

### Examples

```
  messq auth add --auth-file /etc/messq/tokens \
      --id ci-worker --roles publish,consume --streams 'orders*,billing'
```

### Options

```
  -h, --help               help for add

      --roles string       comma-separated subset of publish, consume, admin
      --streams string     comma-separated stream patterns (exact, prefix*, or *)
```
